- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- If sentiment turns bearish sharply (drop >0.50 in recent change), model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to match sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits to recent highs; use 30-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- If news volume drops to 0 for 2+ days, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with low-activity mean.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak and price is trending upward; add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment <0.33 and price > prior 5-day high.
- Forecast bias is strongest in early 30-day window; apply 1–3% downward correction for first 7 days if sentiment is weak or news is low.
